_comment: THE account<->setup table (CLAUDE.md §33/§14, docs/plans/2026-09-19-multi-account.md §0.1). One reader: scripts/mandates.py. A mandate is one customer account attached to one setup: the business is customers renting a methodology and handing over their own account (user decision 2026-09-19), so one account runs several setups across several markets and one setup serves many accounts. That relation is many-to-many and it carries facts of its own -- which version of the setup the customer agreed to, when it started, when it ended, what risk fraction was agreed -- none of which fit in an array field on either side.
_why_setup_version_is_pinned: `setup_version` is the setup's `rule_version` AS IT WAS when the mandate was attached (scripts/setup_version.py: a content digest of the behaviour-deciding inputs, so it moves exactly when behaviour moves). It is pinned, not resolved at run time, because scripts/rank-setups.py rewrites docs/architecture/pilot-top20.json in place: the same setup id can mean different rules next week. A customer keeps running the rules they agreed to until they accept a new version, and mandates.drift() is what makes a divergence visible instead of silent.
_why_empty: Empty is the correct state until there is a real customer. An empty table is not a missing table: scripts/mandates.py validates and answers over zero rows, and the pilot's own accounts are not mandates -- they are the house's own trading, resolved through docs/architecture/pilot-top20.json as before.
_max_accounts_per_method_market_why: User decision 2026-09-19: at most 10 DISTINCT accounts may share ONE methodology on ONE market. Read and enforced by scripts/mandates.py at registry-load time -- a cap on ATTACHMENT, not on positions. It counts across every setup of that method on that market, so attaching a customer to a second ICT setup on crypto does not buy a second allowance: what is bounded is how many customers are exposed to the SAME reading of the SAME market, which is what makes them win and lose together. Deliberately separate from the two gates in scripts/exposure.py, which ask what is on the book right now. This one answers before anybody has a position, which is when the limit is actionable -- the alternative is telling the eleventh customer their signal was refused.
_states_why: PENDING = agreed but not yet trading (credentials not installed, market closed). ACTIVE = the runner may take signals for it. PAUSED = temporarily stopped by us or the customer; positions may still be open, so it is NOT the same as ENDED. ENDED = finished, `ended_at` set, never resumes -- a returning customer gets a new mandate, so the history of what they ran when stays readable.
